text:
Diego Santos: heads up #eng — pushed a batch of changes for the Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) in `redwood-terraform`. We’re trying to get reviews in today/tomorrow so we can unblock the installer integration work.

Diego Santos: PRs up for review:
- PR-247: terraform-docs generation + CI check for README consistency
- PR-248: checkov/tflint CI jobs + suppression policy
- PR-249: integration test harness (ephemeral plan/apply) w/ region + NAT mode matrix
- PR-250: wrapper module `modules/redwood-private-vpc` composing baseline + endpoints + SG; stable outputs contract

Diego Santos: Review checklist (please skim even if you only look at one PR):
1) Interfaces
- Variables have descriptions + sane defaults where appropriate
- Outputs match what installer needs (subnet IDs, endpoint IDs, SG IDs) and names are consistent
- No breaking renames without a migration note

2) Secure-by-default
- No `0.0.0.0/0` ingress in baseline SGs
- Endpoint policies are stubbed safely (deny-by-default if we’re not ready) OR clearly documented if permissive
- Checkov suppressions are minimal + justified w/ a comment (ticket/ADR link)

3) CI + UX
- `terraform fmt` and `validate` run in CI
- tflint config doesn’t block on noisy provider rules
- integration tests are bounded (timeouts, retries, cleanup) + don’t require long-lived secrets

4) Docs
- README gets updated by terraform-docs (don’t hand-edit generated sections)
- Notes on NAT modes (single vs per-AZ) + cost caveats are clear

Diego Santos: If you can only review one: PR-250 is highest leverage (wrapper outputs are what the installer will consume).

(reactions: :eyes: x6, :thumbsup: x4)

Sahana Iyer: :eyes: taking PR-249 + PR-248. quick q: are we settled on the integration test AWS account story? I see role assumption in the harness but want to confirm we’re not baking in static creds anywhere.

Diego Santos: yeah, the harness assumes `AWS_ROLE_ARN` from GitHub OIDC + session name. no static keys. if you spot anything that looks like a leak/footgun pls call it out.

ci-bot: CI run started for redwood-terraform/pr-249 (workflow: terraform)

Irene Choi: I’ll review PR-250 (wrapper). can you call out explicitly which outputs are “contracted” vs “nice to have”? installer folks will treat everything as required if it exists :)

Benji Okafor: +1 on that. we’d like a minimal required set we can validate against. optional outputs are ok but we need to know what to ignore.

Diego Santos: good point. I’ll add a short “Outputs contract” section to the wrapper README + mark required vs optional. also will add `precondition` checks where we can (e.g., endpoints enabled => output present).

Victor Alvarez: grabbing PR-248 (tflint/checkov). pls make sure the tflint ruleset won’t force everyone into provider pinning changes every other week.

Sahana Iyer: re PR-249: saw you added retries for endpoint creation eventual consistency :pray:. did you also cap overall runtime? we should keep the matrix under ~20m or it’ll get ignored.

Diego Santos: yep, job timeout is 25m, each apply step has its own 10m timeout + one retry. and we’re only doing 2 regions in the matrix for now.

Elliot Price: I can review PR-247 (terraform-docs). can we ensure the README template includes the “supported topologies” section? docs site is going to copy/paste that.

Diego Santos: yep, PR-247 adds a required section check (fails CI if README missing headings we list). I’ll confirm “Supported topologies” is included in the required headings.

Bruno Silva: looking at PR-250 now. do we want the wrapper to expose both per-tier subnet IDs AND the flattened list? customers keep asking for “just give me the list.”

Benji Okafor: installer wants tier-specific (private/isolated) because we map components differently. flattened list is fine as convenience but we can’t depend on it.

Diego Santos: agree. wrapper will expose:
- `private_subnet_ids`, `isolated_subnet_ids` (contract)
- `all_subnet_ids` (convenience)

Marcus Lin: I’ll do a quick security pass on PR-250 + PR-248. please double check the checkov skips: if we skip something like “flow logs enabled” we need a doc note + an explicit variable gate (default on).

Victor Alvarez: also saw an endpoint policy placeholder — can we at least ensure it’s not wide open by default? (I know some services require permissive policies to function, but we should be explicit.)

Diego Santos: current default is AWS-managed endpoint policy for S3 gateway, and for interface endpoints we don’t attach a custom policy by default (AWS default). we can add a note that customers can pass in explicit JSON policies for stricter control.

Sahana Iyer: PR-248 nit: can we standardize suppression format to include `reason:` and either `ADR:` or `ENG:` link? makes auditing later way easier.

Diego Santos: +1, I’ll update suppression policy doc + fix the existing ones in the PR.

github: Diego Santos pushed commits to redwood-terraform/pr-248 (2 new commits)

github: Diego Santos pushed commits to redwood-terraform/pr-250 (1 new commit)

Irene Choi: reviewed PR-250. overall LGTM. main ask: add a guardrail for the “existing VPC” mode so we don’t accidentally create endpoints in a different VPC than the provided subnets. I left a comment.

Diego Santos: thanks — good catch. will add validation that `vpc_id` matches the subnet VPC when consuming existing subnets (via data lookup).

Elliot Price: PR-247 looks good. I left one comment: the required headings check should be tolerant to docs site links (some READMEs have a “Docs:” section). otherwise +1.

Marcus Lin: PR-248: suppressions look reasonable after your update. please add one line in the README: “checkov failures are treated as build failures; suppressions require justification + link” (people will ask).

Diego Santos: will do.

Diego Santos: ty all. pinging again for reviewers on PR-249 (integration harness) if anyone has cycles — especially folks who’ve been burned by flaky AWS endpoint creation. :)

(reactions: :raised_hands: x3, :white_check_mark: x2)
